thesis: This episode argues that PAR is a compelling 'amazing American entrepreneurial story' that successfully transitioned from hardware to software, particularly through the acquisition of BRIC which achieved true product market fit. The speaker, who joined the board in April 2018, highlights that while the product was winning, the company was historically structured for failure with no money on its balance sheet, leading to bad decisions. The core investment view is that PAR represents a model for buying assets in growth-ish software businesses, contrasting its culture and margins with those of Amazon and Google.

claims.claim: The speaker describes PAR as an 'amazing American entrepreneurial story' that transitioned from hardware to software but notes the market cap was lower than the IPO valuation 40 years ago.
claims.quote: So PAR is an really amazing American entrepreneurial story. The company was founded over 50 years ago in the mid or late 1960s as a defense contractor. Par stands for pattern analysis recognition. Par was Palantir for Palantir. It had this idea that you could use data to predict the future.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that PAR's market cap was lower than its IPO valuation 40 years ago due to missing the software transition.
claims.quote: People's joke that when I stepped into PAR, the market cap of PAR was lower than the IPO valuation 40 years ago, or right around there. And so it was a massive loss share of the value. And the reason was that PAR was never able to get in the software business. It had missed that transition.

claims.claim: The speaker describes PAR's transition to a software business as successful after acquiring BRIC, which grew from 300 to 9 or 10,000 stores.
claims.quote: And within five years, it worked. The business went from being in 300 stores to 9 or 10,000 and really cemented this idea that PAR is now transitioning to a software business. And so that's right around where I got involved.
